title: Notification Planning — Strategic Communication

fields.headline: Notification Plan: Who, When, What
fields.narration: The facilitator stands at the head of the room and addresses the team. 'You've now heard the full scope of the breach — PII, operational data, the ASP, and the PACS blueprint. You’ve reviewed the options: Scorch the Earth, Strike Surgically, or Monitor and Contain. Now, you must decide how to communicate. The clock is running. Your first responsibility is to protect the airport’s reputation, maintain trust, and comply with legal obligations. Begin drafting your notification timeline. Who gets informed first? When do you tell employees? When do you go public? What do you say to the airlines? How do you report to TSA about the ASP? Do you notify passengers whose data may have been in the AODB? And who will write the official breach letter — and what will it say? This is not a technical issue. This is a leadership decision. The public will expect clarity. The airlines will expect action. Your response must be precise, coordinated, and timely. Begin now.'
keyFacts: TSA requires a formal report on ASP compromise within 24 hours.
Employees must be notified of PII breach within 72 hours under state law.
Passenger data exposure may trigger federal breach notification requirements.
Airlines demand written assurance on data integrity by end of day.
The official breach letter must be approved by Security-Legal and signed by the Ops Director.
fields.expectedAction: Team builds a prioritized notification timeline, with legal, compliance, and public messaging roles clearly assigned. The PIO drafts the employee notification, and the SLC drafts the TSA report.
fields.facilitatorNote: This inject sets the stage for the final phase of decision-making. Watch for who takes ownership of communication, and whether legal/Compliance is actively shaping the message. Ensure the timeline is realistic and aligned with real-world regulatory windows.
fields.scenarioTitle: The Long Game — Scenario 2: Advanced Persistent Threat

instructorNote: This inject drives the team to operationalize their strategic choices. Watch for alignment between legal, communications, and operations. The timeline must reflect real regulatory and stakeholder timing, not just internal preferences.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.quote: Ops coordinates and communicates. LEO controls queues; TSA re-opens checkpoints; LEO/Security sweep the sterile area first. Airlines re-staff and inform passengers. CBP re-establishes FIS.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Emergency Plan (AEP)
citations.headingPath: AEP › Part I › Section 3 › 3.4 Capability Assessment
citations.quote: **A. Airport Capabilities (Initial Response).** Fire/Rescue: Index B ARFF (2 trucks, 3,000+ gallons water/foam); response to runway mid-point <3 minutes. Law Enforcement: Airport Police Department, 4

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.quote: - All Staff: RUN. HIDE. FIGHT.; call 911 or ACC with shooter location/description when safe. - LEO/Security: assume IC; contact teams; establish cold/warm/hot zones; declare scene secure for EMS. - Op
